title: Compare Y and Z in Python
description: This code shows that Z supplies recursion under Python's call-by-value evaluation while classical Y fails before invoking its generator.

steps.description: The code identifies Python as call-by-value, defines classical Y, and defines Z with an extra lambda around self-application.
fact_gen receives recursion as self rather than naming itself. Z supplies that self-reference to build factorial.

steps.question: Can the same Z combinator provide recursion to a Fibonacci generator with two recursive calls?
steps.answer: Yes. The code applies Z to fib_gen and evaluates fib(10).

steps.description: fib_gen uses self twice in its recursive case, and Z supplies the required recursive function.
The code lowers Python's recursion limit and tries to build Y(fact_gen). It catches RecursionError because Y fails before f runs even once.
The comments state the expected factorial, Fibonacci, and Y failure outputs.
